paragraphs.source_en:
29 January to 13 March, with their present more spacious accommodation on the upper
floor of the same house where they have been installed for just over three weeks. If ‘this
month’ is taken to mean the previous four weeks or so, rather than the month of April, and
to approximate the time (23 days) since they entered their new apartments, S. would have
resumed ‘literary occupations’ in early to mid-March and so probably composed SP before
the end of the month. If, however, by ‘this month’ April is meant, then he would have
composed SP in the month following Mary’s date in Harvard Nbk 1. Just over two years
after the letter to Hunt of April 1820, S. again wrote to him on 19 June 1822 from Lerici;
in the letter, he refers to Jane Williams, whom he expected Hunt soon to meet as ‘a most
delightful person — whom we all agree is the exact antitype of the lady I described in the
Sensitive plant — though this must have been a pure anticipated cognition as it was written
